Bibliometric analysis identified three key research hotspots: the association between UPF intake and cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs); the association between UPF consumption and early cardiometabolic impairment in children and adolescents; and mechanisms underlying food matrix disruption and food additive-mediated cardiometabolic dysregulation. Conclusion Global research interest in the relationship between UPF intake and cardiometabolic health has grown substantially over the past decade. This study provides a comprehensive mapping of the current research landscape, key hotspots, and emerging frontiers in this field, offering a valuable reference for future investigations and public health interventions.

title: When less is more: Unifinal framing promotes intention to use social media for social connection
abstract: People often wish to rekindle their dormant relationships yet struggle to act on their intentions. This intention-action gap is notable in an era of rising loneliness and surprising in a time marked by unprecedented technological tools for social connection. We propose that one reason for this gap lies in how people evaluate the appropriateness of the means for achieving their social connection goals. Drawing on goal systems theory, we examined whether framing social media platforms as serving a single social connection goal (unifinality) versus multiple goals (multifinality) shapes evaluations of the means and intentions to reconnect with dormant ties. Across three preregistered studies ( N = 1095), unifinal framing increased perceived diagnosticity—the sense that a means is well suited to a focal goal—which in turn enhanced intentions to reconnect. Diagnosticity was empirically distinguishable from perceived instrumentality and more consistently accounted for the effect of framing on intentions to reconnect. These findings highlight goal structure as a key determinant of when people view digital platforms as appropriate tools for meaningful social connection and when they intend to use them for such purposes. We discuss broader implications for how individuals navigate their social goals in increasingly multifinal digital environments and for how technology companies must balance emphasizing multifunctionality with highlighting specific relational affordances.

title: Trends in hepatitis B virus seroprevalence in a large cohort of adult cancer patients from 2010 to 2023
abstract: PURPOSE: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection poses increased risks for cancer patients due to immunosuppression and potential viral reactivation. We evaluated the seroprevalence and temporal trends of HBV exposure in a large cohort of cancer patients in Brazil. METHODS: Adult patients who underwent anti-HBc testing at a quaternary oncology center between 2010 and 2023 were included in this retrospective study, and HBV exposure was defined as anti-HBc positivity. Temporal trends were assessed by using linear regression, whereas associated factors were evaluated by using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Anti-HBc testing was performed in 22.9% (28,869/125,985) of admitted cancer patients, and seroprevalence was 13.4% (3,857/28,869), declining from 16.5 in 2010 to 9.9% in 2023 (p < 0.001). Decreasing trends were observed across sexes and age groups (p < 0.001 for both), with a more pronounced decline among men (25.1%-12.3%). Seroprevalence also decreased significantly among White patients (16.7%-7.9%; p < 0.001) and those with solid tumors (18.8%-9.0%; p < 0.001), but not among non-White individuals (21.4%-17.7%; p = 0.246) or those with hematological malignancies (13.1%-12.8%; p = 0.136). Age ≥ 60 years (OR = 4.40; 95%CI: 3.77-5.12; p < 0.001), men (OR = 1.89; 95%CI: 1.76-2.04; p < 0.001), and non-White ethnicity/color (OR = 1.25; 95%CI: 1.15-1.35; p < 0.001) were independently associated with HBV exposure. CONCLUSION: Despite the declining seroprevalence over time, HBV exposure remains common among cancer patients, as persistent disparities across demographic groups underscore the need for expanded vaccination and systematic screening.

title: Long-Term Perspective on the Landscape of Recognized and Unrecognized Myocardial Infarction
Mechanisms of accelerated biological aging and premature cardiovascular events in young and middle-aged post-COVID-19 survivors
Genetic predisposition to Kawasaki disease and the risk of coronary atherosclerosis: a Mendelian randomisation study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease is linked to coronary artery abnormalities, yet whether this reflects a direct causal relationship with atherosclerosis remains unclear due to potential confounding factors. This study aimed to investigate, using two-sample Mendelian randomisation, whether a genetic predisposition to Kawasaki disease is associated with subsequent atherosclerosis. METHODS: Instrumental variables were single-nucleotide polymorphisms significantly associated with Kawasaki disease from a large-scale genome-wide association study (119 cases, 6071 controls). Summary data for coronary atherosclerosis (the primary outcome), cerebral atherosclerosis, peripheral atherosclerosis, and three non-invasive surrogates (brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, and pulse wave arterial stiffness index) were obtained from independent European and African cohorts. The inverse variance weighted method served as the primary analysis, supported by four sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: = 0.01), This direction was consistent across all sensitivity methods, with no evidence of pleiotropy or heterogeneity. No associations were observed for the remaining outcomes. Reverse analysis did not support reverse causality. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that genetic predisposition to Kawasaki disease may be associated with coronary atherosclerosis. Given the limited cohorts, the null findings for other vascular territories are inconclusive. Larger independent Kawasaki disease genome-wide association studies are needed for replication.

title: The role of nurses in cardiovascular disease secondary prevention: partnering with patients in cardiac rehabilitation and digital health
abstract: ABSTRACT Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, underscoring the importance of effective secondary prevention. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach integrating exercise training, patient education, cardiovascular risk-factor modification, and behavioral support. Despite its established benefits, CR remains substantially underutilized because of barriers at the patient, clinician, organizational, and health-system levels. This article examines the importance of nurses partnering with patients across the CR continuum to advance patient-centered education and communication, shared decision-making, behavior change, and long-term self-management. First, we describe CR as a model of comprehensive secondary prevention and examine barriers to referral, enrollment, participation, and equitable access, including challenges relevant to resource-limited settings. Second, we focus on patient education and counseling as interactive, individualized processes that expand beyond information provision to build patients’ knowledge, skills, confidence, and capacity for behavior change and self-management. We highlight nursing strategies including assessment of learning needs and readiness for change, health-literacy-responsive communication, teach-back, motivational interviewing, tailored counseling, shared decision-making, and collaborative goal setting. Third, we consider how digital health technologies can extend patient education, communication, self-monitoring, and feedback within and beyond traditional CR settings, and discuss emerging applications and current limitations of artificial intelligence. Finally, we identify priorities for nursing practice, including improving identification and referral, strengthening education and communication, promoting patient partnership, expanding equitable access, appropriately integrating technology, and supporting the transition from CR to lifelong secondary prevention. Across these domains, nurses are well-positioned to integrate clinical expertise with patient-centered education and communication, partnering with patients and families to address barriers, support informed decision-making, and facilitate sustained behavior change. Digital and AI technologies have the potential to extend these partnerships beyond traditional CR settings. Strengthening these partnerships across the CR continuum can support the transition from structured CR to long-term self-management and lifelong cardiovascular health.

title: Aldosterone synthase inhibitors may alter how primary care treats hypertension
abstract: Hypertension guidelines recommend adding antihypertensive therapies until the blood pressure (BP) is below a specific target. If the BP is not below target with 3 medications, including a diuretic, then it is labeled resistant hypertension, and then we investigate for secondary causes, such as primary aldosteronism (PA). PA testing seems complex with 3 results: aldosterone, renin, and the aldosterone-renin ratio. Hence, these tests are ordered infrequently, and the diagnosis of PA is often delayed or never made. Also, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and other conditions can have elevated aldosterone, which are not PA-related. The traditional treatment with aldosterone receptor blockers/mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists has been helpful, but they block the effects that are mediated through the mineralocorticoid receptor. The non-receptor effects of high aldosterone may continue to cause harm. Therefore, blocking the production of aldosterone with an aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI) could be a more complete strategy to address elevated aldosterone levels. In addition, an "ASI Challenge" may help us decide which patients need formal testing for PA. If the systolic blood pressure drops a significant amount (>10 mm Hg), then that suggests aldosterone is a key component of the uncontrolled BP, and those patients should be considered for formal PA testing. For those who drop a modest amount (<10 mm Hg), they would be less likely to need PA testing. Such an approach could use an ASI agent as a diagnostic/screening tool as well as a therapeutic agent, which would be very helpful in the primary care setting.

title: The NLRP3 inflammasome as a bridge between myocardial infarction and depression: mechanisms, bidirectional link, and therapeutic potential
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) and depression frequently co-occur and form a bidirectional relationship that worsens patient outcomes, with inflammation serving as a core mechanism linking these two disorders. The NLRP3 inflammasome, a key component of the innate immune system, plays a pivotal role in sterile inflammatory responses. This review systematically summarizes the structural characteristics, activation mechanisms, and pathophysiological functions of the NLRP3 inflammasome, with a particular focus on its involvement in the pathogenesis of MI and depression and the bidirectional relationship between the two diseases. We comprehensively elaborate on the role of the NLRP3 inflammasome as a molecular bridge between MI and depression, exploring mechanisms including oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, ATP-P2X7 signaling and calcium pathways, peripheral and central inflammation, sympathetic and vagus nerve pathways, the gut microbiota-gut-brain axis, neurotransmitter and neurotrophic metabolic dysregulation, VEGF-mediated vascular permeability, metabolic disturbances, and neuroendocrine dysfunction. We also discuss the clinical implications of NLRP3-related molecules as biomarkers for predicting treatment responses and analyze the role of the NLRP3 inflammasome in treatment sensitivity and resistance within heart-brain comorbidity. Finally, we summarize current therapeutic strategies targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome and propose future research directions. We propose that NLRP3 inflammasome activation is a common upstream driver of both cardiac remodeling and depressive neuroinflammation, and that its persistence explains why standard therapies often fail in comorbid patients. Targeting NLRP3 may therefore break the self-sustaining inflammatory loop that perpetuates the comorbidity. Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome may represent a novel strategy for breaking the vicious cycle between MI and depression, offering potential benefits for both cardiovascular and mental health. Importantly, direct evidence for NLRP3 as a causal mediator in comorbidity-specific systems remains limited; we therefore present this as an integrative framework that synthesizes parallel pathways and identifies critical knowledge gaps.

title: Pharmacologic Stress Myocardial Perfusion Imaging with SPECT and PET in Liver Transplant Candidates: Physiologic Limitations, Current Evidence, and Future Directions
Portopulmonary hypertension: an integrated approach to diagnosis, risk stratification, and management
abstract: Portopulmonary hypertension (PoPH) is a complex and underrecognized form of pulmonary arterial hypertension arising in the setting of portal hypertension, in which outcomes are driven by the interplay between pulmonary vascular disease and liver dysfunction. Despite advances in hemodynamic definitions and targeted therapies, PoPH remains associated with significant morbidity and mortality, largely due to delayed diagnosis, challenges in risk stratification, and the absence of disease-specific management strategies. Recent insights support a paradigm shift from a purely hemodynamic view toward an integrated model encompassing pulmonary vascular load, right ventricular adaptation and hepatic reserve. This multidimensional framework has important implications for screening, prognostic assessment and therapeutic decision-making, particularly in the context of liver transplantation, where treatment is increasingly aimed at achieving transplant eligibility. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and clinically oriented overview of PoPH, integrating current evidence on pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification and management. We highlight key limitations of existing approaches, discuss emerging therapeutic strategies and propose a conceptual framework to guide clinical practice and future research in this challenging condition.

title: Transformer models in cardiovascular medicine: current applications, translational challenges, and future directions
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide, highlighting the need for improved early detection, accurate diagnosis, and personalized therapeutic strategies. With advances in artificial intelligence (AI), Transformer-based models have attracted increasing interest because they can model long-range dependencies, support large-scale pre-training, and integrate heterogeneous data. Originally developed for natural language processing, Transformers have been extended to medical image analysis, physiological signal interpretation, and clinical text mining. In cardiovascular medicine, these models have been applied to electrocardiogram interpretation, cardiac imaging, electronic health record analysis, multimodal data integration, digital-twin development, and large language model-enabled workflows. Although many studies report promising performance, clinical value remains contingent on data quality, external validation, calibration, workflow integration, and trustworthy governance. This narrative review provides a focused overview of Transformer-based models in cardiovascular medicine, critically evaluates their translational limitations, and outlines priorities for clinically useful and responsible cardiovascular AI.

title: Health Care Expenditures and Cost-Sharing Before and After Long COVID: Three-Year Evidence From a Statewide Multi-Payer Cohort
abstract: The objective of this study was to quantify expenditures for long COVID (LC) before/after diagnosis and compare 3-year trajectories with similar patients without LC in claims. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using Colorado All Payer Claims Database multi-payer claims (October 1, 2020-August 1, 2024). Adults with ≥1 U09.9 code and 1-year continuous enrollment pre-index were followed 1 year pre- and 2 years post-index. Multipart models addressed right-censoring; clustered bootstraps produced confidence intervals overall and by age, sex, and payer. Sample: 25,229 LC and 126,089 comparison patients across commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, and dual coverage. LC patients averaged $79,777 total expenditures over 3 years and $5,158 in cost-sharing. Spending rose about 6 months before the index date, peaked just before the index date, and returned to baseline within 6 months; excess spending totaled $21,597 per patient. Dual-eligible patients had the highest absolute expenditures but lowest relative increase, whereas Medicaid had the lowest absolute expenditures and highest relative increase. LC patients had a substantial financial burden concentrated around diagnosis, highlighting broader, system-level implications for health care spending.

title: The role of serine/arginine-rich splicing factors in cardiovascular diseases
Self-reported memory problems as a sequela of post-COVID-19 condition: A systematic review
[18F]ApaScan: A 2-Pyridinylbenzimidazole PET Tracer with Highly Selective Binding to Human Aldosterone-Producing Adenoma Tissue
abstract: Abstract Aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) is overexpressed in aldosterone-producing adenomas (APAs) and represents a promising PET target for the noninvasive localization of APA lesions in primary aldosteronism. To address this need, we synthesized and evaluated 2-pyridinylbenzimidazole analogues for their ability to bind to human APA (hAPA) tissue. Based on initial binding assays, five analogues were selected and radiolabeled with fluorine-18 for autoradiographic and saturation binding studies. Among them, [18F]3 ([18F]ApaScan) exhibited high-affinity binding to hAPA homogenates (KD = 8.4 nM) with no measurable specific binding to normal adrenal (hNA) homogenates, demonstrating excellent tissue selectivity for hAPA over hNA. Quantitative autoradiography using [18F]3 further confirmed a high hAPA-to-hNA tissue binding ratio of 18. In normal rats, [18F]3 displayed rapid adrenal uptake, efficient clearance without prolonged retention, and no skeletal accumulation. Taken together, these results suggest that [18F]3 has the potential to be developed into a PET tracer for localizing APAs in primary aldosteronism.

title: Safety of Antibacterial Agents in Liver Transplantation: A Review of Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Aspects
abstract: INTRODUCTION. Alterations in hepatic and renal function, systemic inflammation, and immunosuppressive therapy in liver transplant recipients significantly modify the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles of antibacterial agents, necessitating optimization of their dosing strategies. AIM. To systematize the available evidence on the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics and drug–drug interaction potential of antibacterial agents in patients after liver transplantation in order to clarify the safety profile of antibacterial therapy. DISCUSSION. The literature analysis demonstrated that the incidence of infectious complications after liver transplantation reaches 41.3%, with up to 21.7% of cases being caused by multidrug-resistant strains. In the early posttransplant period, changes in the volume of distribution, plasma protein binding, and clearance of antibacterial agents determine the variability of systemic exposure and hinder the attainment of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic targets, increasing the risk of treatment failure and drug toxicity. Clinically significant drug–drug interactions between macrolides (clarithromycin, erythromycin) and calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) as well as inhibitors of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) (sirolimus, everolimus) are associated with increased concentrations of immunosuppressants and an increased risk of toxic reactions. The principal adverse reactions are hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and hematologic and neurologic complications, the risk of which increases with polypharmacy and impaired renal function. CONCLUSIONS. The pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic variability of antibacterial agents in liver transplant recipients necessitates a personalized approach. The use of therapeutic drug monitoring of β-lactam antibiotics, vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and linezolid, along with the consideration of drug–drug interactions, can improve the efficacy and safety of antibacterial therapy in patients after liver transplantation.

title: The Clinical Utility of Adding Laminin Gamma 2 Monomer to the PAGE‐B Score for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Surveillance in Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A residual risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) persists despite the use of nucleos(t)ide analogs (NA) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. We aimed to assess the utility of baseline serum laminin gamma 2 monomer (LG2m) by integrating PAGE-B score to predict HCC. METHODS: NA-treated CHB patients whose baseline serum LG2m, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and PAGE-B score were measured. We evaluated the predictive value of LG2m in subgroups stratified by cirrhosis status and PAGE-B score and proposed a HCC surveillance algorithm. RESULTS: HCC developed in 56 of 1016 patients over a follow-up of 3651 person-years (annual incidence: 1.53%). None of the low PAGE-B patients developed HCC over 5 years. LG2m did not significantly stratify risk in high PAGE-B patients. Conversely, LG2m was significantly predictive of HCC in nonhigh PAGE-B patients (5-year incidence: 5.5% vs. 1.0% for high vs. low LG2m, p = 0.004). Integrating LG2m, AFP, and high PAGE-B achieved a sensitivity of 98.2% for HCC detection. Among patients with a nonhigh PAGE-B score, elevated LG2m was associated with a higher risk of HCC (adjusted HR, 4.40; 95% CI, 1.26-15.44), whereas AFP did not significantly stratify HCC risk in a separate analysis. Intermediate PAGE-B patients with high LG2m should receive closer HCC surveillance (annual incidence: 1.4%) as with high PAGE-B patients did (annual incidence: 1.9%). CONCLUSION: Serum LG2m level was predictive of HCC specifically among patients with intermediate PAGE-B score. Integration of LG2m into a PAGE-B-oriented algorithm provides a biomarker-driven tool for individualized surveillance, which is vital for improving early-stage HCC detection.

title: Die neuen Aldosteronsynthaseinhibitoren
abstract: Zusammenfassung Aldosteron ist in der Hypertoniebehandlung lange vor allem mit primärem Hyperaldosteronismus und resistenter Hypertonie verknüpft worden. Inzwischen mehren sich die Hinweise, dass „Aldosteronexzesse“ deutlich häufiger zur Blutdruckerhöhung und Organschädigung beitragen als bislang angenommen, sodass teilweise ein Screening auf Hyperaldosteronismus bei allen Hypertonikern empfohlen wird. Die Diagnostik und therapeutischen Möglichkeiten dieser Zustände sind im klinischen Alltag herausfordernd und bisweilen unzureichend. Neue Aldosteronsynthaseinhibitoren (ASI) versprechen einen direkteren Eingriff in diese Pathophysiologie und könnten ein pragmatisches Werkzeug für den Umgang mit Zuständen von Aldosteronexzessen bieten. In den letzten beiden Jahren sind einige klinische Daten über den Einsatz von ASI entstanden, die einen Ausblick auf ihre künftige Rolle im Management von kardiovaskulären Erkrankungen ermöglichen. Wir diskutieren im Folgenden die aktuellen Entwicklungen, das Potenzial und die Limitationen dieser neuen Medikamentenklasse über die reine Blutdrucktherapie hinaus.

title: Adherence to European AIDS clinical society hepatitis B management guidelines in people with HIV: real-world evidence from Spain and Germany
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate adherence to hepatitis B virus (HBV) management recommendations among people with HIV (PWH) and chronic HBV infection. DESIGN: A multicenter cross-sectional study. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study in 42 centers in Spain and Germany between June 2024 and March 2025. Chronic HBV infection was defined as at least two positive hepatitis B surface antigen tests obtained more than 6 months apart. Adherence to 2023 European AIDS Clinical Society recommendations regarding anti-HBV treatment, liver enzyme monitoring, HBV-DNA testing, antihepatitis D virus (HDV) screening, and HDV-RNA confirmation was assessed. Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance was evaluated separately and has been reported elsewhere. RESULTS: A total of 1235 PWH with chronic HBV infection were included. The median age was 56 years, 84% were men, and 36% were born outside Europe. Overall, 88% had HIV-RNA less than 50 copies/ml, and the median CD4+ cell count was 623 cells/μl. Among participants with available HBV-DNA result, 87% had undetectable HBV-DNA. Guideline-recommended anti-HBV treatment was documented in 88% of individuals. During the previous 12 months, liver enzyme monitoring was performed in 94% and HBV-DNA testing in 71%. Overall, 81% had ever undergone anti-HDV testing and, among anti-HDV-positive individuals, 66% had undergone HDV-RNA testing. CONCLUSION: Although adherence to several components of HBV care was high, gaps remain in the implementation of current recommendations for PWH, particularly in HBV-DNA monitoring and HDV evaluation. Better integration of these measures into routine HIV care may improve long-term prevention of liver-related complications.

title: Changes in triglyceride-glucose index and progression of coronary artery calcification in asymptomatic adults: a longitudinal cohort study
abstract: Introduction The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a readily available surrogate marker of insulin resistance; however, the association between changes in TyG index and coronary artery calcification (CAC) progression remains unclear. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 14,407 Korean adults without cardiovascular disease who underwent two baseline examinations during 2012–2018 and at least three examinations overall. At each baseline examination, TyG index status was classified as low or high using a predefined cutoff, yielding low-to-low (L-L), low-to-high (L-H), high-to-low (H-L), and high-to-high (H-H) groups. CAC progression was defined as a difference of ≥2.5 between the square root-transformed coronary artery calcium score (CACS) of the follow-up and index examination. Cox proportional hazards and linear mixed-effects models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 5-year fold changes, respectively. Results During a median follow-up of 5.34 years, 4,139 participants experienced CAC progression. Compared with the L-L group, the risk of CAC progression increased across the L-H, H-L, and H-H groups, with adjusted HRs (95% confidence intervals) of 1.07 (0.96–1.19), 1.14 (1.02–1.27), and 1.30 (1.20–1.41), respectively. Associations differed between CAC subgroups ( p for interaction <0.001), with more pronounced associations observed among participants with CACS of zero at both the first and index examinations. The 5-year fold change was 11% higher in the L-H group than in the L-L group and 9% lower in the H-L group than in the H-H group. Conclusion Changes in TyG index status were associated with CAC progression, particularly among individuals without detectable CAC. Serial TyG index assessment may aid in cardiovascular risk stratification.

title: Gut Microbiota and Its Metabolites in the Prognosis of Coronary Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Mechanistic Insights
Emotional Comfort at a Cost: The Dynamic Role of Social Chatbot Use in Daily Loneliness, Well-Being, and Interpersonal Interaction
abstract: As generative AI chatbots increasingly serve as emotional companions, understanding their implications for users’ emotional and social lives is critical. This 14-day diary study involving 97 social chatbot users examined how daily loneliness relates to chatbot engagement and subsequent psychosocial outcomes. Bayesian multilevel models showed that on days when participants felt lonelier than usual, they reported longer chatbot use and stronger emotional engagement. Notably, these two forms of engagement showed distinct associations with daily outcomes. Emotional engagement was associated with higher daily subjective well-being but shorter interpersonal interaction duration, whereas longer usage duration was associated with lower interpersonal interaction pleasure. Mediation analyses reflected the same patterns. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing behavioral from emotional engagement with social chatbots and suggest that emotional benefits and interpersonal costs may coexist in everyday human–AI interaction, informing the responsible design and balanced use of social AI companions.

title: PRIMARY ALDOSTERONISM IN GENERAL PRACTICE: TIMELY DIAGNOSIS AS A KEY TO PROBLEM SOLVING
abstract: Objective. The aim of the study is to demonstrate the clinical significance of the timely detection of secondary hypertension in patients with resistant hypertension and severe cardiovascular complications. Materials and Methods. We analyzed a clinical case of a 49-year-old female patient with long-standing resistant hypertension, multiple ischemic strokes, severe hypokalemia, and target organ damage. Clinical and laboratory evaluations were performed, including measurements of aldosterone and renin levels and the aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR). Adrenal imaging was conducted using computed tomography (CT). Results. The patient presented with persistent, poorly controlled hypertension despite multicomponent antihypertensive therapy, chronic severe hypokalemia. Notably, this hypokalemia had long been overlooked and had not prompted either a treatment revision or a targeted diagnostic workup. Additionally, hypernatremia, left ventricular hypertrophy, and sequelae of recurrent ischemic strokes were identified. Hormonal profiling revealed elevated aldosterone levels and an increased aldosterone-to-renin ratio. Computed tomography identified a left adrenal mass consistent with an aldosterone-producing adenoma. The patient underwent endoscopic left adrenalectomy. Postoperative outcomes included normalization of potassium levels, a decrease in aldosterone concentration, restoration of the aldosterone-to-renin ratio, and achievement of target blood pressure levels. It is highly probable that the prolonged, undiagnosed course of primary hyperaldosteronism was a major risk factor for the recurrent acute cerebrovascular events that resulted in the patient's permanent disability. Conclusion. This case highlights a prolonged, undiagnosed course of primary hyperaldosteronism associated with severe cerebrovascular complications and subsequent disability. In routine clinical practice, timely screening for primary hyperaldosteronism using the aldosterone-to-renin ratio in comorbid patients with resistant hypertension and hypokalemia could facilitate early diagnosis and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

title: Integrated physical and mental healthcare for older adults in Europe: from concept to implementation—a joint EuGMS and EAGP perspectives paper
abstract: Older adults commonly experience coexisting mental and physical multimorbidity, alongside frailty and polypharmacy. This clinical complexity is associated with poorer health outcomes, including higher rates of acute hospital admission, longer lengths of stay, increased dependency at discharge and higher mortality. Despite this, physical and mental health services for older adults are fragmented across Europe, often operating in a parallel rather than integrated manner. As a result, many patients receive poorly coordinated care. In response, there is growing interest in the development of integrated care services for these patients across Europe. Although a range of service models have been proposed, what constitutes "best practice" remains unclear and is likely to depend on local population needs, service configuration, healthcare context and healthcare workers education. The European Geriatric Medicine Society and European Association of Geriatric Psychiatry have initiated a Task and Finish Group to develop expert-based recommendations for integrated physical-mental health services for older adults across Europe. In this perspectives paper we consider the challenges associated with delivering integrated physical-mental healthcare for older adults, drawing on clinical and service level observations. We suggest that current approaches to integrated care are often limited in scope and variability and may not fully address the needs of older adults with combined physical and mental illness. A broader conceptualisation of integration may be required. We outline implications for future research, service development, and policy, with a focus on improving alignment between healthcare systems to address the needs of this growing population. This work was endorsed by the European Geriatric Medicine Society.

title: The cholesterol, high‐density lipoprotein, and glucose index and its derivatives related to obesity and inflammation as novel metabolic markers for predicting new‐onset cardiovascular‐liver‐metabolic multimorbidity: A prospective cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-liver-metabolic multimorbidity (CLMM), defined as the co-occurrence of at least two of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, is an increasing health burden. We evaluated the cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index and its obesity- and inflammation-derived variants for predicting incident CLMM. METHODS: This prospective cohort included 6,534 adults aged ≥45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. CHG, eight obesity-derived indices, and CHG-CRP were assessed, with the triglyceride-glucose index and TG/HDL-C ratio as comparators. Associations with incident CLMM were evaluated using logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and threshold analysis. Predictive performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis, the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and the net reclassification improvement (NRI), with additional joint-effect, interaction, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: At the 2015 follow-up, 406 participants (6.2%) met the criteria for CLMM. Higher CHG was linearly associated with incident CLMM (highest vs lowest quartile: OR 1.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-2.22). Obesity-derived variants showed stronger associations, particularly CHG-BMI (OR 3.13, 95% CI 2.21-4.43), which also had the highest discrimination (AUC 0.643, 95% CI 0.616-0.669) and continuous NRI (34.08%). Participants with both high CHG and high BMI had the greatest CLMM risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.94-3.51). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: The CHG index and its obesity-derived variants, particularly CHG-BMI, are accessible and inexpensive candidate metabolic markers for predicting new-onset CLMM. CHG-BMI showed the highest apparent discrimination among the evaluated indices, although its AUC was modest. External population validation is needed.

title: Impact of histologic hepatic steatosis on virological response to nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy in patients with chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B remains a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide. We investigated whether histologic hepatic steatosis affects hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid (HBV DNA) suppression in patients receiving antiviral therapy. This retrospective observational study included 307 adult patients with chronic hepatitis B who received tenofovir or entecavir therapy and underwent pretreatment liver biopsy. Demographic, laboratory, virological, radiological, and histopathological data were retrieved from the electronic medical record system. Laboratory parameters included complete blood count, liver function tests, alpha-fetoprotein, renal function tests, and lipid profile. Histopathological evaluation included fibrosis stage, histologic activity index, and hepatic steatosis percentage. Ultrasonographic findings included hepatic steatosis, liver echotexture, and contour. The primary outcome was HBV DNA suppression at 12 months. Long-term virological response was evaluated as time to first HBV DNA suppression during follow-up (maximum 60 months). A total of 307 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir were included, of whom 258 (84.0%) achieved HBV DNA suppression at 12 months. Patients without suppression had higher baseline aspartate aminotransferase, histologic activity index, histologic steatosis, and baseline log10 HBV DNA levels (all P < .05). Histologic steatosis ≥5% was more frequent in patients without suppression (42.9% vs 23.6%, P = .005). In multivariable analysis, steatosis ≥5% (odds ratio 0.365, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.179-0.746; P = .006) and higher baseline log10 HBV DNA (odds ratio 0.842, 95% CI 0.751-0.944; P = .003) were associated with a lower likelihood of 12-month suppression, with similar findings in the parsimonious sensitivity model. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed delayed suppression with steatosis (log-rank P = .016); however, this association was not significant in the conventional adjusted Cox model (hazard ratio 0.900, 95% CI 0.689-1.175; P = .438), and a significant time-dependent interaction indicated non-proportionality (P < .001). Histologic steatosis and higher baseline log10 HBV DNA were associated with a lower likelihood of 12-month HBV DNA suppression. However, an independent longitudinal association with time to suppression was not demonstrated. Residual confounding by unmeasured metabolic factors cannot be excluded.

title: Adjuvant pegylated interferon-alpha after nucleos(t)ide analog withdrawal drives a temporally coordinated expansion of regulatory B cells and contraction of HBV-specific T cells
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The NUC-B study showed that a 4-month course of pegylated interferon-alpha (PEG-IFNα) enhanced the outcome and reduced hepatic flares following nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) withdrawal in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B. Here, we investigated differential T- and regulatory B-cell (B REG ) changes before and during these interventions in a substudy of 41 representative patients. APPROACH AND RESULTS: Antigen-specific T cells were primarily evaluated using quality-controlled IFN-γ ELISpot with 15 pools of genotype-matched HBV core/small-surface peptides, confirmed by multiparameter flow cytometry. B-cell responses were tested with multiparameter flow cytometry and intracellular IL-10 staining. Broader baseline IFN-γ-producing-HBV-specific T cells correlated with higher sustained off-treatment viral control and reduced flares. PEG-IFNα led to a transient reduction in HBV-specific T cells that persisted for over 1 month after treatment. B REG producing the immunosuppressive cytokine IL-10 expanded more than 5-fold during adjuvant PEG-IFNα. The kinetics of B REG induction correlated with flares in both arms and showed a significant inverse temporal correlation with IFN-γ-producing-HBV-specific T-cell frequencies. CONCLUSIONS: Baseline breadth and magnitude of HBV-specific T cells should be evaluated as biomarkers to select patients more likely to have favorable outcomes with NUC withdrawal ±PEG-IFNα. The expansion of B REG provides insights into homeostatic mechanisms induced by PEG-IFNα and withdrawal flares, which could constrain HBV-specific T cells while limiting inflammation.

title: Night-shift frequency and loneliness among NHS employees: a multi-site cross-sectional analysis of the INTERACT study
Classroom music intervention and first-year student adaptation: the roles of group synchrony, teacher–student relationship quality, and sense of belonging
Human-in-the-loop Reinforcement Learning for personalized and adaptive interventions in wellness and healthcare: A systematic literature review
abstract: Background Reinforcement Learning (RL) is emerging as a promising technique to support personalized and adaptive clinical interventions. This is thanks to its ability to model sequential decision making and to learn from longitudinal data. The deployment of RL raises challenges regarding interpretability and integration into clinical workflows. These concerns have motivated interest in human-in-the-loop approaches, in which individuals retain an actual or intended role before an RL-supported decision affects care. However, the use of RL in healthcare remains fragmented and poorly standardized. A systematic review of the literature is therefore timely, to identify current state, directions, challenges and research gaps. Methods A systematic review was reported in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. ScienceDirect, Scopus, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science databases were searched for all records available up to 21 January 2026, encompassing studies applying RL to personalized interventions in healthcare and wellness fields and including the concept of “human-in-the-loop”. Extracted information contained diseases, applications, RL-methods, dataset dimensions, integration with other techniques, and performance evaluation strategies. Results Forty-one papers met the inclusion criteria and were examined in detail. RL was mainly found in the healthcare rather than in the wellness field, especially in type 2 diabetes and other chronic diseases, and intensive care settings, where the sequential nature of decision-making processes plays a significant role. Data structure and information vary extensively, creating significant comparability challenges. The methodologies show strong heterogeneity in algorithms and evaluation metrics, limiting reproducibility and generalizability. From the disease-focus point of view, cardiovascular applications are underrepresented, despite cardiovascular diseases being the leading cause of death globally and the potential value of adaptive decision-making in cardiovascular disease management. Conclusions RL offers an opportunity to personalize treatments and optimize clinical decision-making processes employing sequential data. However, the lack of shared methodological standards, transparency in model descriptions, and limited number of prospective studies constitute significant barriers to its adoption. In conclusion, better documented datasets, comparable metrics, and prospective evaluations are required to establish clinical effectiveness and support future implementation.

title: Long‐COVID Associated With Incident Hypertension: A Population‐Based Cohort Study
abstract: Background Long COVID has been linked to persistent autonomic and vascular abnormalities, but its impact on hypertension among non‐hospitalized COVID‐19 convalescents remains unclear. Given the link between blood pressure and cardiovascular morbidity, understanding how long COVID modifies the risk of incident hypertension is clinically important. Methods We conducted a longitudinal population‐based study using MIRACLE‐S (Multimorbidity Integrated Registry Across Care Levels in Stockholm). Adults aged 18 to 65 years without prior hypertension or hospitalization for acute COVID‐19 were followed from October 2020 to January 2025. Long COVID was defined by a physician‐assigned U09.9 diagnosis. The outcome was new‐onset hypertension ( International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD‐10] I10). Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs), adjusted for age, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, mental health, and pre‐pandemic health care utilization. Analyses were stratified by sex. Results Among 1 221 570 adults, 8365 (0.7%) were diagnosed with long COVID, and 18% developed incident hypertension during follow‐up. Individuals with long COVID (women: n=5578, 16%; men: n=2787, 24%) showed an early and consistently higher cumulative incidence than unexposed individuals ( P <0.0001). Long COVID was associated with increased hypertension risk overall (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.09–1.20; P <0.001), and in women (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.05–1.22; P =0.001) and men (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.05–1.27; P =0.002), with stable estimates across models. Conclusion Long COVID was associated with elevated risk of incident hypertension in non‐hospitalized COVID‐19 convalescents. These findings suggest SARS‐CoV‐2 infection may contribute to vascular and autonomic dysregulation affecting blood pressure, supporting structured monitoring and risk management in individuals with persistent post‐COVID symptoms.

title: The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health
Ultrasound findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography in patients with chronic hepatitis B in Georgia
Deep-learning analysis suggests a facial image signal associated with low muscle mass in a clinical cohort enriched for chronic liver disease: a proof-of-concept study
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is a clinically relevant complication of chronic liver disease. Because changes in muscle mass, adiposity, and nutritional status may affect facial morphology, this exploratory study examined whether standardized frontal facial photographs contain an algorithmically detectable signal associated with low measured muscle mass. Methods Prospectively collected clinical data and facial photographs from 255 participants were retrospectively analyzed using the 2010 European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP1) framework. The binary target was low versus normal measured muscle mass. Stage 1 developed ImageNet-pretrained VGG16, MobileNetV2, and DenseNet121 models in 204 participants and evaluated them in a 51-participant internal hold-out set. Stage 2 independently redeveloped the task using four region-specific EfficientNet-B0 and DenseNet121 components integrated into a single decision pipeline and evaluated it separately within the same source cohort. A clinical-variable-only comparator, human image assessment, Grad-CAM, and controlled perturbation analyses were also performed. Results Overall, 173 participants had low and 82 had normal muscle mass. Stage-1 balanced accuracy was 0.71 for VGG16, 0.70 for DenseNet121, and 0.63 for MobileNetV2 The integrated stage-2 system showed high sensitivity (94.3%) but limited specificity (50.0%), resulting in a balanced accuracy of 0.72. Human image assessment showed low interrater agreement. Grad-CAM and perturbation analyses indicated contributions from facial regions but also substantial dependence on peripheral and non-face image content. The clinical-variable comparator outperformed the stage-1 facial models. Conclusion Standardized facial photographs contained a image-derived information associated with low measured muscle mass across two independently implemented modelling stages. The integrated stage-2 pipeline achieved high sensitivity, supporting further investigation of facial image analysis as a low-burden pre-screening approach. However, limited specificity, potential clinical and diagnostic-pathway confounding, dependence on non-face image content, and the absence of external validation indicate that these findings remain exploratory. Prospective external validation and assessment of incremental value beyond routine clinical variables are required before clinical implementation.

title: Patient preferences for medicines information in cardiovascular disease and the influence of unmet needs on medication adherence: A cross‐sectional study
abstract: Limited evidence exists on how patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) prefer to receive medicines information and whether having unmet needs influences medication adherence. We conducted a cross-sectional study using national survey data (20/05/2025-25/06/2025) from Australian MedAdvisor application users taking ≥4 CVD medicines. The questionnaire covered demographics, medication adherence (MARS-5), and information needs and preferences. Multivariable linear regression examined associations between unmet information needs and adherence. Among 313 participants (mean age 68.5 years, 38.7% female), 52.4% reported unmet information needs, particularly on drug interactions and side effects/precautions. One third (31.9%) were completely adherent (MARS-5 25/25), while 49.2% were partially adherent (MARS-5 23-24). Most preferred receiving information via electronic messages (45%) or mobile applications (22%). After adjustment, unmet medicine information needs was associated with medication non-adherence (coefficient: -0.83 [95% CI: -1.22, -0.44]). These findings highlight a substantial need for improved medicines information, particularly via digital modalities, to enhance adherence in CVD.

title: Selective inhibition of aldosterone production modulates human adrenocortical (HAC15) cell fate
abstract: Background Aldosterone, produced in the zona glomerulosa (ZG) by aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2), regulates sodium balance and blood pressure. In adult adrenals, CYP11B2-expressing ZG cells are sparse, likely reflecting chronic suppression of the renin–angiotensin system under high-salt conditions. Whether reduced aldosterone synthesis directly influences ZG cell behavior remains unclear. This study examined the impact of CYP11B2 inhibition on human adrenal cell fate and function. Methods CYP11B2 was inhibited in HAC15 cells using siRNA (siCYP11B2) or baxdrostat, a selective CYP11B2 inhibitor. Forty-eight hours post-treatment, steroid hormone levels, RNA sequencing profiles, and functional outputs (EZMTT metabolic assay, xCELLigence real-time cell analysis, and Annexin V/SYTOX flow cytometry for apoptosis/necrosis) were evaluated. Results siCYP11B2 reduced aldosterone production by 70% ± 2.9% ( n = 18, p < 0.001) and suppressed mRNA expression of CYP11B2 (88% ± 10.8%), HNRNPA1 (33% ± 17.6%), and UHMK1 (42% ± 13.7%) ( n = 9, p < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis revealed differential expression signatures enriched in autophagy- and mitophagy-related pathways. Treatment with U0126 (MEK1/2 inhibitor) dose-dependently reduced angiotensin II-stimulated aldosterone and cortisol production ( n = 12, p < 0.001), and SB203580 (p38 MAPK inhibitor) increased the aldosterone-to-cortisol ratio (4.5 ± 0.5-fold, n = 12, p < 0.001), at concentrations previously reported to inhibit (25–50 µM U0126) or induce autophagy (1 µM SB203580), respectively. EZMTT assays demonstrated increased metabolic activity in siCYP11B2-treated cells at 96 h (Δ0.141 ± 0.02 absorbance units, p < 0.001), which was not observed following baxdrostat treatment. Baxdrostat treatment altered overall cell-death responses (FC = 1.42 ± 0.05, n = 144 and p = 1.3 × 10 −10 ); however, the relative distribution of apoptotic and necrotic populations varied across independent experiments. Conclusion Reduced aldosterone synthesis is associated with transcriptional signatures involving autophagy- and mitophagy-related pathways. Pharmacological treatment using U0126 and SB203580 altered steroidogenic output independently of CYP11B2 transcript expression, providing hypothesis-generating evidence linking cellular homeostasis and mitochondrial quality control processes to adrenal steroidogenesis. Furthermore, pharmacological CYP11B2 inhibition using baxdrostat produced variable alterations in cell-death profile, highlighting important considerations for long-term therapeutic targeting.

title: Missed Diagnosis in Alcohol‐Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Call for Alcohol Consumption and Liver Disease Early Detection
abstract: Alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma is an increasingly prevalent consequence of alcohol use and the often-silent progression of alcohol-related liver disease. A substantial proportion of patients with alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma are diagnosed at an advanced stage, frequently because underlying liver disease has not been previously identified and surveillance has not been implemented. This review summarizes recent epidemiological trends and clinical features of alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma, with a particular focus on the high proportion of undiagnosed cirrhosis and the challenges posed by alcohol use disorder, comorbidities and socioeconomic vulnerability. Strengthening collaboration between hepatology and addiction medicine, alongside population-level strategies to reduce alcohol use, will be essential to enhance surveillance uptake and ultimately improve outcomes in alcohol-related hepatocellular carcinoma.

title: Device-aware compensation of nonideal spintronic synapses for electrocardiogram classification using spiking neural networks
abstract: Spintronic synapses offer a promising route toward low-power neuromorphic hardware for edge intelligence. Their nonvolatility, multilevel tunability, and compatibility with event-driven spiking neural networks (SNNs) make them attractive for temporal biomedical signal processing. Moving beyond conventional demonstrations of synaptic plasticity, here we examine how nonideal spin–orbit torque (SOT) synaptic updates affect SNN learning and how they can be compensated. TaMo/CoFeB/MgO/Ta SOT devices with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy exhibit nonvolatile multilevel anomalous Hall resistance states and reversible long-term potentiation and depression. Combined finite-element and micromagnetic simulations indicate that the nonlinear weight evolution is closely associated with spatially nonuniform SOT-driven domain dynamics. Incorporating the measured update curves into an SNN for MIT-BIH electrocardiogram abnormal-beat classification shows that device nonideality strongly degrades recognition of minority-class abnormal beats. A device-aware compensation strategy restores balanced effective updates, bringing the overall accuracy close to the ideal-update reference (95.06% vs 95.23%). It also increases the F1 score for the minority F-class abnormal beats from 11.86% to 64.08%. This work highlights device-aware compensation as an effective route for translating nonideal spintronic synapses into practical low-power biomedical neuromorphic hardware. Such hardware is promising for wearable health-monitoring applications.

title: The liver–gut–bone axis in hepatic osteodystrophy: mechanisms, clinical evidence and therapeutic perspectives
abstract: Hepatic osteodystrophy (HOD) is an important but under-recognized complication of chronic liver disease (CLD), characterized by reduced bone mass, impaired bone microarchitecture and increased fragility fracture risk. Its skeletal phenotype and pathogenic mechanisms vary substantially according to CLD aetiology and disease stage. In metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), skeletal risk is closely associated with metabolic dysfunction and hepatic fibrosis; alcohol-associated liver disease combines direct ethanol-related osteotoxicity with malnutrition and endocrine abnormalities; viral hepatitis-associated bone disease is influenced by persistent inflammation, disease stage and antiviral exposure; and cholestatic liver diseases are characterized by disrupted bile acid homeostasis, fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption and impaired bone formation. The liver–gut–bone axis provides an integrative framework linking these disease-specific features. Gut dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbial translocation and altered metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acids and tryptophan-derived metabolites, may contribute to abnormal bone remodelling through inflammatory, metabolic and nutritional pathways. Cirrhosis further amplifies skeletal injury through sarcopenia, malnutrition and endocrine dysfunction. However, human evidence establishing a complete causal liver–gut–bone pathway remains limited. Current management should therefore focus on treatment of the underlying liver disease, fracture-risk assessment, nutritional and lifestyle interventions and evidence-based anti-osteoporotic therapy, while microbiota- and metabolite-targeted strategies remain investigational. Future prospective studies integrating microbiome and metabolomic profiling with bone turnover, microarchitecture and fracture outcomes are needed to clarify causal mechanisms and improve individualized management of CLD-associated HOD.

title: Potential under-recognition of primary aldosteronism in young adults with hypertension
Liver Transplantation for Alcohol-Related Liver Disease in 2026: Phenotypes, Selection, and Post-Transplant Care
abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) for alcohol-related liver disease (ArLD) has evolved from a pathway centered on decompensated cirrhosis and prolonged abstinence to one that also encompasses severe alcohol-related hepatitis (sAH) and alcohol-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). This change reflects the growing burden of ArLD and evidence that carefully selected patients with acute presentations can achieve excellent post-transplant survival. The traditional six-month abstinence rule has limited value as a stand-alone predictor of harmful post-transplant alcohol use. International guidance increasingly supports individualized multidisciplinary assessment of alcohol use disorder (AUD), psychiatric comorbidity, social vulnerability, insight, and treatment engagement, although listing requirements remain heterogeneous. Abstinence nevertheless remains a disease-modifying intervention that may promote clinical improvement, hepatic recompensation, and delisting in selected candidates. After LT, long-term care should integrate prevention and treatment of harmful alcohol use with surveillance and management of graft-related, cardiometabolic, oncologic, infectious, and other medical complications. This narrative Perspective critically appraises LT for ArLD in 2026 and proposes a phenotype-informed framework integrating medical urgency, dynamic reassessment, alcohol-use biomarkers, and longitudinal transplant–addiction care.

title: Toll-like receptor 7 and interferon-α synergy establishes a positive feedback loop to potentiate antiviral immunity in chronic hepatitis B
PUS7 pseudouridylation of 7SK orchestrates human somatic cell reprogramming into iPS cells
abstract: Reprogramming human somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells) provides huge potential for regenerative medicine but its molecular regulation remains incompletely understood. In this study, we identify PUS7 as an RNA modification checkpoint that promotes acquisition of pluripotency. PUS7 loss markedly impairs reprogramming, whereas its overexpression accelerates reprogramming efficiency and kinetics. Mechanistically, PUS7 pseudouridylates U250 of the chromatin-associated noncoding RNA 7SK, enhancing its interaction with the BRG/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complex. Loss of this modification disrupts 7SK-BAF association, reduces BAF chromatin occupancy and decreases global chromatin accessibility. We further establish PSKM (PUS7, SOX2, KLF4, MYC) reprogramming, which generates iPS cells with faithful imprinting, robust lineage potential and improved developmental fidelity. PSKM-iPS cells differentiate efficiently toward neural and hematopoietic lineages and undergo gastrulation-like morphogenesis. These findings link 7SK pseudouridylation to chromatin remodeling and establish PSKM as a framework for generating high-quality human iPS cells for modeling and regenerative medicine.

title: Apport de l'élastométrie impulsionnelle (FibroScan®) dans l'évaluation de la fibrose hépatique chez les patients atteints d'hépatopathies virales chroniques B et C: étude transversale au Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sourô Sanou, Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso
abstract: Introduction: les hépatopathies virales chroniques B et C constituent un problème de santé publique majeur au Burkina Faso. L'élastométrie impulsionnelle (FibroScan®) est une méthode non invasive permettant une évaluation précise de la fibrose hépatique. Cette étude visait à analyser l'apport du FibroScan® dans l'évaluation de la fibrose hépatique et son impact sur les décisions thérapeutiques chez les patients atteints d'hépatopathies virales chroniques B et C au Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sourô Sanou (CHUSS). Méthodes: il s'agissait d'une étude transversale à visée diagnostique, à collecte rétrospective des données, menée au service d'Hépato-Gastroentérologie du CHUSS de Bobo-Dioulasso entre le 6 janvier 2023 et le 10 avril 2025. Ont été inclus les patients de 15 ans ou plus, atteints d'hépatite B ou C chronique documentée, ayant bénéficié d'un FibroScan® valide et d'un bilan biologique complet. La performance diagnostique du FibroScan® a été évaluée en termes de classification du stade de fibrose selon METAVIR. L'accord entre FibroScan® et Fib-4 pour la décision thérapeutique a été évalué par le coefficient kappa (Κ) de Cohen. Résultats: au total, 221 patients ont été inclus: 197 (89,1%) atteints d'hépatite B chronique, 24 (10,9%) d'hépatite C chronique et 1 coinfecté VIH/VHB. L'âge moyen était de 36,6 ± 9,8 ans avec une légère prédominance féminine (51,1%). La valeur moyenne du FibroScan® était de 5,9 ± 2,4 kPa. Une fibrose absente ou minime (F0-F1) était présente chez 84,2% des patients. Le FibroScan® a identifié une fibrose significative (≥ F2) chez 15,8% des patients. La concordance entre FibroScan® et Fib-4 était faible dans l'hépatite B (Κ = 0,14; p = 0,05) et modérée dans l'hépatite C (Κ = 0,58; p = 0,003). Le FibroScan® a identifié 56 patients supplémentaires (25,3% de la cohorte) nécessitant un traitement antiviral non détectés par le Fib-4, principalement dans le groupe AgHBe négatif avec fibrose absente au Fib-4 (p < 0,001). Conclusion: le FibroScan® constitue un outil de référence fiable pour l'évaluation de la fibrose hépatique et permet d'optimiser les décisions thérapeutiques dans notre contexte. Son utilisation, en complémentarité avec le Fib-4, est recommandée dans une stratégie séquentielle adaptée aux ressources limitées.

title: Molecular Prevalence of Human Astrovirus Among Children Under Five Years of Age With Gastroenteritis in Ilorin Metropolis, North‐Central Nigeria: A Cross‐Sectional Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Human astrovirus (HAstV) is a recognized cause of viral gastroenteritis, however, data from north‐central Nigeria remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of classic HAstV RNA and explore associated factors among children under 5 years presenting with gastroenteritis in Ilorin, Nigeria. Methods This hospital‐based cross‐sectional study was conducted from May 2025 to September 2025 among 200 children aged 13–59 months attending selected hospitals in Ilorin who presented consecutively. Stool samples were collected and analyzed using real‐time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction for classic HAstV RNA. Data were analyzed using R software. Participant characteristics were summarized descriptively, prevalence estimates were calculated with exact 95% confidence intervals, and associations with astrovirus detection were evaluated using Fisher's exact test, the Wilcoxon rank‐sum test, and Firth penalized logistic regression. Results Classic HAstV RNA was detected in 4 of 200 children under 5 years with acute gastroenteritis, giving an overall prevalence of 2.0% (4/200; 95% CI: 0.55%–5.04%). Prevalence was highest among children aged 49–60 months (2.94%), males (2.50%), rural residents (2.33%), users of borehole/well water (2.86%), and children attending daycare (4.0%). All astrovirus‐positive children presented with vomiting, moderate dehydration, resided in rural communities, had animal contact, used borehole/well water, and received oral rehydration solution. No other characteristics were significantly associated with HAstV. Feeding method was the only factor significantly associated with detection ( p = 0.03), with the highest prevalence among exclusively breastfed children (33.3%; 2/6). However, wide confidence intervals around both the raw prevalence and the adjusted odds ratio (aOR = 0.01; 95% CI: 0.00–0.29) indicate this finding is exploratory rather than confirmed, warranting confirmation in larger studies. Conclusion Astrovirus in this population is relatively low; however, it remains epidemiologically important, particularly as prevalence may vary with season. Continued surveillance and further molecular characterization are warranted.

title: Evaluating the potential of treatment options for chronic hepatitis B
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide, but long-term or even lifelong viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) seldom clears hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), so-called 'functional cure.' In recent years, a shift in treatment strategy from viral suppression toward cure has emerged, catalyzed by three revised international hepatitis B guidelines (2025-2026) and the first-in-class phase 3 evidence that a finite antiviral therapy, the antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen, can achieve a functional cure in about one in five NA-suppressed CHB patients with baseline HBsAg below 3000 IU/mL. AREAS COVERED: We evaluated the spectrum of established and emerging treatment options for CHB, organized around quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) as the axis for selecting and sequencing therapy. Coverage spans backbone NAs and pegylated interferon-α, an HBsAg-guided roadmap, finite NA therapy and off-treatment outcomes, bepirovirsen, other virus-targeting and immunomodulatory agents, and genome-directed covalently closed circular DNA silencing and editing. EXPERT OPINION: Bepirovirsen's approaching approval is an inflection point. qHBsAg should guide personalized, sequential therapy, with partial cure (HBsAg <100 IU/mL) as a potential intermediate target when functional cure is unlikely. Durability, standardized biomarkers, rational combination design, metabolic co-management and equitable access are the priorities; a sterilizing cure remains distant.

title: Reclaiming health: a qualitative, explorative study of long covid recovery journeys involving mind-body approaches.
abstract: ABSTRACT Post-covid-19 condition (long COVID) involves multiple organ systems, causes prolonged functional impairment, and places a substantial burden on individuals and healthcare systems. In light of self-reported recovery stories following mind-body approaches on social media, and lack of empirical studies thereof, this study explores these narratives of recovery journeys. Eighteen adult women (aged 37-62 years), with self-reported lived experience of substantial recovery from long COVID through mind-body approaches, were asked to retrospectively reflect on their recovery process in semi-structured interviews. Using inductive thematic analysis, we systematically traced and compared elements and patterns within the recovery journeys . Despite heterogeneity in symptoms and pathways, a shared non-linear and iterative recovery trajectory emerged, resulting in five common elements and patterns: 1) encountering a new explanation for their long COVID symptoms, centred on nervous system dysregulation; 2) navigating a way into mind-body approaches; 3) a fundamental reorientation, resulting in hope, a change in therapeutic approach and acceptance; 4) experiential learning to apply mind-body techniques; and 5) evaluation of and reflection on the process and factors that influenced it. These processes resemble findings from research on mind-body approaches in chronic pain and fatigue conditions. Most participants navigated recovery with little or no formal clinical support, relying instead on online communities while actively avoiding information that conflicted with their new understanding. Participants' experiences unfolded within a highly contested environment characterised by competing understandings of long COVID. Such narratives are not merely descriptive but may shape illness beliefs, healthcare-seeking behaviour, treatment expectations and recovery trajectories.

title: The Aldosterone–Immune Axis in Primary Aldosteronism: Linking Adrenal Pathogenesis to Systemic Inflammation and Target-Organ Damage
abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is the most common endocrine cause of secondary hypertension and is increasingly recognised as a systemic disorder extending beyond haemodynamic dysregulation. Accumulating evidence suggests that chronic autonomous aldosterone excess promotes maladaptive immune activation, establishing an aldosterone–immune axis that may contribute to cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic injury independently of blood pressure elevation. In some patients, glucocorticoid co-secretion may further amplify tissue-specific mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) signalling. Human and experimental studies indicate that aldosterone modulates both innate and adaptive immunity. Patients with PA demonstrate altered monocyte transcriptional profiles, enhanced vascular inflammatory activity, and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine signalling in monocyte-derived macrophages compared with blood-pressure-matched essential hypertension controls. Experimental models further show that sustained aldosterone exposure promotes macrophage M1 polarisation, dendritic cell activation, Th17 expansion, and regulatory T-cell suppression. These inflammatory changes are accompanied by oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, fibroblast activation, and extracellular matrix remodelling across cardiovascular and renal tissues. Emerging evidence is also consistent with a role for trained innate immunity, whereby prolonged aldosterone exposure may induce persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of monocytes and macrophages. Whether such reprogramming persists after biochemical correction by adrenalectomy or MR antagonism in human PA has not yet been directly demonstrated and remains an important open question. If confirmed, these mechanisms may help explain the partial irreversibility of target-organ damage despite successful treatment. This review synthesises current evidence linking adrenal somatic pathogenesis to systemic immune dysregulation and target-organ injury in PA. We propose that PA should be viewed not solely as a hypertensive disorder, but as a chronic fibro-inflammatory endocrine disease with important implications for early diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted therapy. Future prospective human studies are needed to confirm the mechanistic hierarchy proposed and to identify the immunological targets most amenable to therapeutic intervention.

title: Tislelizumab-induced immune-mediated hepatotoxicity combined with two episodes of hepatitis B virus reactivation: a case report
abstract: Immune-mediated hepatotoxicity (IMH) is a typical immune-related adverse event associated with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), while hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) is an infectious complication that may also occur during ICI therapy. However, these two conditions are usually independent and rarely co-occur in the same individual. Herein, we describe a patient with lung squamous cell carcinoma who developed HBVr and IMH simultaneously after receiving tislelizumab, and the co-existence of two episodes of HBVr brings challenges to the diagnosis and treatment of IMH. In the diagnosis of IMH, the co-existence of HBVr masked the underlying IMH, resulting in a delay in IMH treatment. In the treatment of IMH, the re-occurrence of HBVr led to a dilemma of continuing to use glucocorticoids (GCs) or stopping them. In such a clinical scenario, the multidisciplinary approach, close monitoring of liver function and HBV-DNA, and a carefully balanced treatment strategy combining GCs with intensified antiviral therapy are essential to realize the optimal management for IMH. In conclusion, medical staff should be alert to the coexistence of HBVr and IMH in patients receiving ICIs, so as to avoid missed diagnosis and treatment delay.

title: Language-supervised electrocardiogram interpretation with vision transformer
abstract: Purpose: Most artificial intelligence models for electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation rely on task-specific supervised learning, requiring dedicated labeled datasets for each diagnostic task and limiting scalability across diverse cardiac conditions. This study investigated whether vision-language learning from paired ECG recordings and summary reports could enable transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. Methods: We developed ECG-VLM, a contrastive vision-language model consisting of a Transformer-based image encoder and a text encoder, trained on 800,034 paired 10-s ECG recordings and summary reports from the MIMIC-IV-ECG database. Cardiac condition detection was performed using natural-language prompts without condition-specific retraining or fine-tuning. Performance was evaluated on an internal test set and externally validated using the LSAS-ECG dataset (45,151 recordings) across 14 cardiac conditions, together with retrieval and subgroup analysis. Results: ECG-VLM achieved diagnostic performance across 14 cardiac conditions, with AUROC ranging from 0.679 to 0.981 on the internal test set and from 0.691 to 0.991 on external validation. Performance was strongest for rhythm abnormalities (mean AUROC 0.948 internally and 0.921 externally) and lower for morphological conditions. Compared with the previously reported signal-based ECG-CLIP framework, ECG-VLM achieved comparable performance for rhythm abnormalities while improving AUPRC for several morphological conditions. Performance remained broadly consistent across external validation and demographic and clinical subgroups. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of vision-language supervision from paired ECG recordings and summary reports for learning transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. This framework provides a basis for future extension of vision-language learning to ECG images encountered in routine clinical practice. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00482-7.

title: Programmed cell death in inflammation: interactions and holistic perspective
abstract: Programmed cell death (PCD) is a major regulatory mechanism that maintains tissue homeostasis and immune balance and strongly influences the initiation, progression and resolution of inflammation. Although apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis and ferroptosis are individual PCD modes that are regulated by different molecular mechanisms, they are not mutually exclusive in inflammatory microenvironments. Instead, these pathways are linked via common signaling mediators and regulatory nodes that enable crosstalk, compensatory activation and context-dependent fine-tuning. It is evident that apoptosis, pyroptosis and necroptosis can be coordinated within defined inflammatory platforms, as exemplified by concepts such as PANoptosis. Pathway-specific modeling is inadequate for inflammatory diseases involving multiple PCD modalities, metabolic and organelle stress, immune-cell interactions and tissue-level changes that molecular models cannot capture. Here, an integrated cell death network (ICDN) paradigm is presented as an organizational schema describing how various types of PCD are coregulated through common regulatory pathways in inflamed tissues. This framework does not identify a new mode of cell death per se but rather integrates pathway compensation following extracellular perturbations, disease-specific inflammatory responses, and susceptibility to therapeutic intervention at common network nodes. This review defines the molecular mechanisms and crosstalk of inflammatory pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis pathways; links recent advances in death modality applications for specific diseases to the ICDN framework; and highlights important current limitations that require further examination, including the need for stronger evidence of dynamic switching across cell death modalities, spatial architecture during inflammation, and reconfiguration at both the multiprotein complex and network levels, such as inflammasome networks.

title: Physical Activity and Sedentary Time in Chronic Stroke: An Agreement Study Between the IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph Measures
abstract: BackgroundThe International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form (IPAQ-SF) and ActiGraph accelerometers are widely used and internationally recommended to assess physical activity (PA) and sedentary time (ST). However, their agreement in individuals with chronic stroke remains unclear.ObjectivesTo quantify the magnitude of agreement between IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived weekly moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), total PA, and ST in chronic stroke survivors.MethodsFifty community-dwelling adults with chronic stroke who walked independently were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Participants wore an accelerometer (ActiGraph GT3X+) on the non-paretic side of the waist for seven consecutive days. The IPAQ-SF was completed via interview on the following day.ResultsIPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived estimates showed substantial individual-level discrepancies, with wide limits of agreement (LoA) across outcomes. For MVPA, the mean ratio was 1.02 (95%CI: 0.49 to 2.11; ratio LoA: 0.01 to 154.62). For total PA, the median ratio was 0.08 (95% CI: 0.06 to 0.14; non-parametric ratio LoA: 0.00 to 1.33). For ST, the mean ratio was 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92; ratio LoA: 0.47 to 1.53).ConclusionFindings indicate poor individual-level agreement between the IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived estimates, with wide LoA and evidence of heteroscedasticity. At the group level, the IPAQ-SF underestimated total PA and ST, whereas MVPA showed no evidence of fixed bias. Although the IPAQ-SF may provide a broad descriptive assessment of PA and ST at the group level, it should not be used interchangeably with ActiGraph for individual-level estimation in individuals with chronic stroke.

title: Mechanism-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review
abstract: Background Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment. Objectives To systematically synthesise evidence across the principal causes of secondary hypertension using a mechanism → diagnosis → therapy framework; to compare diagnostic performance and cause-directed treatment effects; and to examine concordance between contemporary society guidelines and real-world implementation. Methods This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, with diagnostic accuracy reporting informed by PRISMA-DTA. MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to 30 June 2025, supplemented by citation searching. The formal search identified 580 records; after removal of 168 duplicates, 412 records were screened, 106 full-text reports were assessed, and 58 included evidence records were represented across 63 publications.
