The review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Screening, extraction and structured appraisal were performed by a single reviewer (the first author); therefore, no dual-reviewer agreement statistic was applicable. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUADAS-2, and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate, and certainty was summarised using GRADE. A targeted post-search surveillance update through 31 July 2026 was used only to contextualise major newly available guidelines and Phase 3 trial reports and did not alter the original PRISMA counts. Results Primary aldosteronism (PA) is best understood as a continuum of renin-independent aldosterone excess: in Brown et al. [The unrecognized prevalence of primary aldosteronism: a cross-sectional study. Ann Intern Med . (2020) 173 :10–20], biochemically overt autonomous aldosterone production was present in 11.3%, 15.7%, 21.6%, and 22.0% across normotensive, stage 1, stage 2, and resistant-hypertension strata, respectively. In unilateral PA, the PASO cohort distinguished complete biochemical success after adrenalectomy (94%; 656/699) from complete clinical success (37%; 259/705), with partial clinical improvement in a further 47%. PATHWAY-2 established spironolactone as the most effective fourth-line drug in resistant hypertension; CORAL, ASTRAL, STAR, and DRASTIC did not support routine revascularisation for stable atherosclerotic renal-artery stenosis; plasma-free metanephrines remained highly sensitive for phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma; and PA testing in eligible patients with resistant hypertension remained only 1.6%–2.1%. Post-search Phase 3 trials of selective aldosterone synthase inhibition showed approximately 9 mm Hg placebo-corrected office systolic blood pressure reductions, but cardiovascular-outcome benefit has not been established, and electrolyte/renal monitoring remains necessary. Conclusions Across secondary hypertension, a limited set of pathophysiological effector pathways maps to specific diagnostic tests and cause-directed treatments. The strongest opportunities for clinical gain are earlier recognition of high-yield phenotypes, accurate aetiological subtyping, and implementation of established testing pathways; emerging aldosterone synthase inhibitors expand blood-pressure-lowering options but should not yet be interpreted as proven cardiovascular-outcome therapies.

title: Application of Extracellular Vesicles in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Diseases
abstract: Paracrine signalling is considered an important mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of cell-based therapies in cardiovascular diseases. Consequently, research in regenerative medicine has increasingly shifted its focus beyond conventional cell-based therapeutic strategies toward cell-derived and cell-free therapeutic approaches. Among these, extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as important mediators of intercellular communication, delivering a diverse cargo of bioactive molecules, including microRNAs, proteins, lipids, and cytokines. EVs have been implicated in several biological processes such as inflammation, angiogenesis, and the response to ischaemic tissue injury. Preclinical studies have demonstrated promising regenerative effects of EV-based therapies in ischaemic cardiovascular diseases, particularly myocardial infarction and chronic limb-threatening ischaemia. However, substantial methodological and translational challenges remain, and robust evidence from prospective randomised clinical trials is required to facilitate their translation into routine clinical practice. In addition to their therapeutic potential, the presence of EVs in biological fluids makes them promising candidates for non-invasive diagnostic and prognostic applications in cardiovascular medicine. This review summarises current evidence on EVs in cardiovascular disease, highlights their potential as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, and discusses emerging therapeutic strategies and the challenges associated with their clinical translation.

title: Self-reported long COVID associated with sleep problems and poor sleep quality among adults in Germany: results of the German Health Update 2023 (GEDA 2023)
abstract: Introduction Long COVID refers to various long-term health impairments following a SARS-CoV-2 infection, including physical, cognitive, and psychological symptoms. Sleep problems are among the most prevalent neuropsychiatric symptoms of long COVID and can negatively affect daily functioning and quality of life. This study aims to investigate sleep onset problems, problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality in associations with long COVID among adults in Germany. Methods Analyses are based on data from the cross-sectional nationwide telephone interview survey “German Health Update” (GEDA 2023). Between March 2023 and February 2024, 9,310 adults (50.8% female, median age = 60.8 years) answered questions on any prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID status, as well as on sleep onset problems, problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality over the past 4 weeks. Weighted prevalence estimates for each sleep variable were calculated by self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID status. Multivariable logistic regressions were conducted, adjusted for age, sex, level of education, chronic conditions, depressive symptoms, COVID-19 vaccination status, and multiple SARS-CoV-2 infections. Results Participants with self-reported current long COVID reported higher proportions of sleep onset problems (32.6%), problems maintaining sleep (47.8%) and poor sleep quality (44.8%) compared to participants without a SARS-CoV-2 infection (20.0%, 30.8 and 24.1%, respectively) or prior infected participants without long COVID (13.8%, 23.8 and 20.0%, respectively). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, participants with self-reported current long COVID had an increased likelihood of experiencing problems maintaining sleep (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.73; 95% CI = 1.23–2.44) and a higher likelihood of poor sleep quality (aOR = 1.81; 95% CI = 1.29–2.55) compared to non-infected individuals; however, sleep onset problems were not associated with long COVID. Discussion Our findings from general population data suggest that adults with current long COVID have 1.7- to 1.8-fold higher odds of problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality than non-infected individuals. Given the potential impact on quality of life and physical and psychological functioning, sleep-related symptoms may represent an important target for clinical assessment and management in individuals with long COVID.

title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids
abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

title: Transplant-Free Recovery in Wilson Disease–Associated Acute Liver Failure
abstract: Wilson disease-associated acute liver failure carries high mortality without urgent liver transplantation. Diagnosis is challenging when classical signs like Kayser-Fleischer rings are absent. We report a 28-year-old woman presenting with Wilson disease-associated acute liver failure characterized by Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia, profound hyperbilirubinemia, low alkaline phosphatase, and a New Wilson Index score of 14. Despite predicting poor transplant-free survival, she achieved complete clinical and biochemical recovery following aggressive copper-removal therapy using chelation, zinc, therapeutic plasma exchange, and continuous renal replacement therapy. This case demonstrates that early combined extracorporeal liver support can successfully bridge patients to recovery, potentially obviating liver transplantation.

title: The Most Recent European and American Guidelines on Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Lack of Focus on Diaphragm Training
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death and morbidity worldwide. Patients with vascular and cardiac conditions undergo cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a process that may begin before surgery (less frequently), after invasive procedures, or as part of chronic disease management, with durations varying by healthcare facilities or national policies. CR is a valuable non-pharmacological intervention that supports patient health and the resumption of daily activities. These rehabilitation programmes are strongly recommended for cardiac patients and are structured according to guidelines from organisations such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the American Heart Association/American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation (AHA/AACPR). This editorial reviews the latest ESC and AHA/AACPR guidelines, emphasising physical activities such as endurance and resistance training, while highlighting the lack of detail on inspiratory muscle training (IMT). The editorial reiterates the Italian Association of Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC) proposals regarding IMT and calls for further clinical trials.

title: Pre-Transplant Laboratory Parameters and Early Outcomes in HBV-Related Deceased Donor Liver Transplantation
abstract: Background: Early postoperative outcomes after deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) are influenced by recipient, donor, and perioperative factors. Routinely available pre-transplant laboratory tests may provide complementary information for risk assessment. This study aimed to explore associations between routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters and early postoperative outcomes after DDLT. Methods: This retrospective single-center descriptive pilot study included 32 adult recipients who underwent DDLT for hepatitis B virus-related liver disease between 2004 and 2019. Pre-transplant biochemical and hematologic parameters were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, biliary complications, infectious complications, bleeding, and hospital stay. Descriptive group comparisons and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: In-hospital mortality occurred in 6/32 recipients (18.8%), biliary complications in 5/32 (15.6%), infectious complications in 9/32 (28.1%), and postoperative bleeding in 2/32 (6.2%). Routine laboratory parameters did not significantly discriminate mortality. Among 28 recipients with available potassium measurements, four developed biliary complications. Potassium showed exploratory discrimination for biliary complications (AUC = 0.818, p = 0.048), based on only four biliary events. Bilirubin and GGT did not significantly discriminate mortality. Conclusions: Routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters showed no consistent association with in-hospital mortality after DDLT. The potassium association is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

title: Artificial intelligence in cardiovascular imaging and electrocardiography
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is reshaping cardiovascular imaging and electrocardiography (ECG) by enabling automated acquisition support, quantification, disease detection, and risk prediction. Yet, high retrospective accuracy does not by itself establish transportability or clinical benefit. This narrative review first outlines the AI development lifecycle, with emphasis on data and label quality, architecture selection, patient-level data partitioning, calibration, external validation, and prospective evaluation. It then critically examines representative advances in ECG, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), cardiac computed tomography (CT), and nuclear cardiology. Particular attention is given to three rapidly evolving areas: AI-enhanced ECG, video- and vision-language echocardiography, and volumetric CT and CMR analysis. We compare convolutional, transformer-based, hybrid, and generative approaches; summarize explainable-AI methods, including gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), integrated gradients, and occlusion testing; and analyze failure modes arising from label, sampling, demographic, device, and temporal bias. Quantitative examples show that performance can deteriorate across institutions, demographic groups, and acquisition settings despite apparently strong internal validation. Future progress will depend on prospective workflow-based trials, multimodal foundation models with transparent benchmarks, lifecycle governance and regulation, and continuous post-deployment surveillance.

title: Precision medicine for resistant hypertension: integrating molecular phenotyping, gut microbiome, device therapy and digital care
abstract: Abstract Resistant hypertension confers substantial cardiovascular and renal risk. However, apparent treatment resistance often arises from reversible problems rather than a discrete biological disease. Precision management starts with confirming true resistant hypertension through standardized office measurement, out-of-office evaluation, validation of treatment adequacy and medication exposure, adherence assessment, and screening for secondary causes. Mechanism-driven phenotyping further identifies treatable pathogenic drivers. Primary aldosteronism, characterized by autonomous aldosterone excess, renin suppression, and sodium retention, serves as the best-defined prototype. Other contributors, including chronic kidney disease, obstructive sleep apnea, sympathetic overactivity, vascular and immune-metabolic dysfunction, and gut microbiome–metabolite pathways, remain at different stages of clinical translation. Phenotypic characterization guides optimized diuretic and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist regimens, selected targeted agents, appropriate device therapies, continuous safety monitoring and long-term care. Digital monitoring, team-based care, registries and learning health systems support adherence optimization, treatment titration, safety surveillance and equitable care access. The overarching aim is to progress from simplistic diagnostic labels to validated clinical phenotyping, personalized treatment matching, and sustained blood pressure control.

title: Factors Associated with Suicidal Ideation Among Middle-Aged Korean Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2022–2023 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
abstract: Background/Objectives: Suicide became the leading cause of death among Korean adults in their 40s in 2024. We identified sociodemographic, health behavior, and mental health correlates of suicidal ideation in mid-life without adjustment for depression, which overlaps with the outcome through Patient Health Questionnaire-9 item 9 and was measured in only one of the two survey years. Methods: This cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 9th Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2022–2023) used complete data from 4715 of 5153 adults aged 40–64 years. Anxiety symptoms were assessed with the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale (screening threshold ≥ 10). Complex-sample logistic regression incorporated strata, clusters, and pooled weights, with all covariates prespecified. Results: Suicidal ideation prevalence was 3.8%. Independent correlates were high perceived stress (odds ratio (OR) = 8.54, 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.47–13.34), one-generation other-type household (OR = 6.81, 3.29–14.08; n = 59, 11 events), elevated anxiety symptoms (OR = 5.01, 3.02–8.32), middle school education or below (OR = 2.13, 1.12–4.03), economic inactivity (OR = 1.85, 1.25–2.73), poor perceived health (OR = 1.70, 1.13–2.55), and low household income (OR = 1.57, 1.08–2.28). Wave-specific adjustment for depression attenuated the stress and anxiety associations by 15–55% without eliminating them. Conclusions: Mid-life suicidal ideation was associated with mental health vulnerability, household composition, and socioeconomic disadvantage. The value of these cross-sectional associations for screening or risk stratification requires prospective evaluation.

title: Gut-liver axis dysregulation and restoration in decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis: rationale and research progress of fecal microbiota transplantation
abstract: Decompensated hepatitis B virus (HBV) related cirrhosis is associated with high mortality and a wide range of complications. Current antiviral and symptomatic treatments fail to reverse core pathological alterations, including disruption of the gut microbial ecosystem. Gut-liver axis imbalance represents a central hub in disease progression. Gut dysbiosis compromises the intestinal mucosal barrier, leading to endotoxin translocation into the bloodstream, which in turn exacerbates hepatic inflammation and fibrosis, thereby establishing a vicious cycle. This review synthesizes the key mechanisms, clinical efficacy, administration routes, and safety profile of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in this disease. It also identifies current technical bottlenecks and research gaps in FMT application and discusses future directions toward precision based and standardized clinical translation of this therapeutic approach.

title: An Adrenal Adenoma as the Culprit Behind 30 Years of Recurrent Syncope
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a treatable endocrine cause of secondary hypertension and, rarely, ventricular tachycardia (VT), syncope, or sudden cardiac death. CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman with hypertension presented with recurrent syncope for 30 years, worsening over 2 weeks. Electrocardiogram showed multifocal premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), with one dominant morphology triggering predominantly monomorphic VT, plus corrected QT interval prolongation. Hypokalemia, renal potassium wasting, left ventricular enlargement, and mild systolic dysfunction were also present. Ventricular arrhythmias recurred despite electrolyte repletion, beta-blocker therapy, and radiofrequency catheter ablation. A positive saline infusion test and a 3.6-cm left adrenal adenoma supported PA. After adrenalectomy, potassium normalized, palpitations improved, VT burden decreased, and syncope did not recur at 1 month. DISCUSSION: PA may present primarily with ventricular arrhythmias and syncope. In patients with ventricular arrhythmias accompanied by hypertension and hypokalemia, PA should be considered as a treatable endocrine-metabolic cause.

title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus‐Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients
abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 59.2% and 72.1% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

title: Characterization of the polymorphic dense granule protein DG11 in Cryptosporidium parvum
Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
abstract: Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point-of-care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics-based dual-mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle-antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein-containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false-negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus-associated toxins and PMA-treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein-based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF-based dual-mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.
